mainTopic: Rules of חליפין, the meaning of אסימון, and the argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש over whether money or משיכה acquires movable items.
overview: The גמרא finishes reading a phrase word by word to learn which items can be used for חליפין. Coins and איסורי הנאה are ruled out, and there are two versions of which word teaches what. Next it asks what the משנה's אסימון is. רב says it is a bathhouse token, but two ברייתות about מעשר שני show that a token and an אסימון are different things. So רבי יוחנן explains that an אסימון is a blank coin, which fits his teaching that רבי דוסא and רבי ישמעאל agree. Then the גמרא turns to משיכה. רבי יוחנן says money acquires by Torah law and משיכה is a rabbinic גזירה, so the seller will save the goods from an accidental fire. ריש לקיש says משיכה comes from the Torah, and they argue over how to read the פסוק of אונאה. The גמרא then challenges ריש לקיש from רבי שמעון and from the curse of מי שפרע in the משנה. It begins to question the answer about the curse with a ברייתא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The word 'to acquire' rejects לוי's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes excluding date pits, then explains that the word 'to acquire' teaches that the vessel used in חליפין is not the seller's, against לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...with date pits. 'To acquire' comes to exclude the view of לוי, who says the חליפין is done with the vessel of the one giving ownership. It teaches us 'to acquire' and not 'to give ownership.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is going through a phrase word by word to learn the rules of חליפין. Here it finishes one point and explains what the word 'to acquire' teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known argument about whose vessel is used in חליפין. לוי says it is the vessel of the מקנה, the one giving ownership. The phrase says 'to acquire' and not 'to give ownership,' so it argues against לוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Date pits, a nearly worthless item
To give ownership to someone else

phrases.english: with date pits.
'To acquire' comes to exclude the view of Levi,
who says it is done with the vessel of the one giving ownership;
it teaches us 'to acquire'
and not 'to give ownership.'
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets belongs to the corrected wording, and it makes the word mean 'to give ownership.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the word-by-word reading that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The vessel used in חליפין is used 'to acquire,' not as the מקנה's vessel, which goes against לוי.

steps.title: What the word 'with it' excludes
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says 'with it' excludes a coin. רב זביד (or רב אשי) says it excludes איסורי הנאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'With it': רב פפא said, it comes to exclude a coin. And רב זביד, and some say רב אשי, said: it comes to exclude items that are forbidden for any benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next word, 'with it,' and gives two opinions on what it rules out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree the word limits what can be used for חליפין. They only argue about what it limits. רב פפא says a coin cannot be used, and רב זביד says איסורי הנאה cannot be used.

phrases.english: 'With it': Rav Pappa said:
to exclude a coin.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב זְבִיד, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר:
phrases.english: And Rav Zevid, and some say Rav Ashi, said:
to exclude items forbidden for benefit.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּיהּ רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר לְמַעוֹטֵי מַטְבֵּעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next word in the same word-by-word reading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'With it' excludes a coin (רב פפא) or איסורי הנאה (רב זביד / רב אשי).

steps.title: A second version of who learns what
steps.stepSummary: In the איכא דאמרי version, 'with it' excludes a coin, 'that is fit' excludes איסורי הנאה, and date pits need no word to exclude them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: 'With it': רב פפא said, to exclude a coin. 'That is fit': רב זביד, and some say רב אשי, said, to exclude items forbidden for benefit. But date pits did not need to be excluded.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of the same discussion. In this version, רב פפא and רב זביד do not argue. Each one learns his point from a different word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, 'that is fit' seems to have been used to rule out date pits. Here that word is used for איסורי הנאה instead. Date pits do not need any word at all, because they are obviously worthless.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument. It is the same discussion told a different way. In this version the two אמוראים can both be right, since they use different words.
steps.whatToRemember: Coins and איסורי הנאה cannot be used for חליפין. Whether date pits needed their own word depends on which version you follow.

phrases.english: Some say:
'With it': Rav Pappa said:
to exclude a coin.

phrases.aramaic: ״דְּכָשַׁר״ – אָמַר רַב זְבִיד, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: 'That is fit': Rav Zevid, and some say Rav Ashi, said:
to exclude items forbidden for benefit.
But date pits did not need to be excluded.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Retells steps 1–2 in a different version.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'With it' excludes a coin, 'that is fit' excludes איסורי הנאה, and date pits need no exclusion.

steps.title: What is an אסימון?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's line 'an אסימון acquires the coin' and asks what an אסימון is.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'An אסימון acquires the coin,' etc. What is an אסימון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes the משנה and asks what the word אסימון means. This sets up רב's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before we can understand the rule in the משנה, we need to know what kind of object an אסימון is.

keyTerms.meaning: A word in the משנה for an unusual kind of coin; its meaning is being asked about

phrases.english: 'An asimon acquires the coin,' etc.
What is an 'asimon'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: goes back to the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word אסימון in the משנה.

steps.title: רב: bathhouse tokens
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that an אסימון is a coin given as a token for the bathhouse.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: coins that are given as a token for the bathhouse.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question. An אסימון is a token you got for entering the bathhouse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב, an אסימון is not regular money. It is a token used as a sign for bathhouse entry. The next step will challenge this definition.

phrases.english: Rav said:
coins given as a token for the bathhouse.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מָעוֹת הַנִּיתָּנוֹת בְּסִימָן לְבֵית הַמֶּרְחָץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An אסימון is a coin given as a token for the bathhouse.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists them as two things
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא about מעשר שני mentions both 'אסימון' and 'bathhouse tokens,' so they seem to be two different things, against רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: We do not redeem מעשר שני on an אסימון, nor on coins given as a token for the bathhouse. This shows that an אסימון is not the same as bathhouse tokens!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב from a ברייתא. The ברייתא names the two items separately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If an אסימון were the same as a bathhouse token, the ברייתא would not need to list both. Naming both shows they are different, which goes against רב's definition.

keyTerms.meaning: Redeem, moving the holiness onto money
Second tithe, which can be redeemed onto coins

phrases.english: They challenged:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְחַלְּלִין מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי עַל אֲסִימוֹן
phrases.english: We do not redeem second tithe on an asimon

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא עַל מָעוֹת הַנִּיתָּנוֹת בְּסִימָן לְבֵית הַמֶּרְחָץ.
phrases.english: nor on coins given as a token for the bathhouse.
This shows that an asimon

phrases.aramaic: לָאו מָעוֹת הַנִּיתָּנוֹת בְּסִימָן לְבֵית הַמֶּרְחָץ!
phrases.english: is not the coins given as a token for the bathhouse!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's definition from step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's definition of אסימון as a bathhouse token.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists the two items separately, so they must be different things.

steps.title: It cannot be an explanation
steps.stepSummary: Someone might say the ברייתא's second phrase only explains the word 'אסימון.' Another ברייתא rules this out: there, רבי דוסא and חכמים argue about an אסימון but agree about bathhouse tokens.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say the ברייתא is just explaining the word, wasn't it taught this way: We redeem מעשר שני on an אסימון, says רבי דוסא, and חכמים say we do not redeem. And they agree that we do not redeem on coins given as a token for the bathhouse!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks a possible defense of רב and makes the challenge stronger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The defense would be that 'nor on bathhouse tokens' just explains what an אסימון is. But in the second ברייתא, the two items have different laws. There is an argument about an אסימון, while everyone agrees about bathhouse tokens. So they cannot be the same thing, and the challenge to רב stands; step 8 gives a new definition.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shuts the easy way out. In step 8 the גמרא drops רב's definition and gives a new one.

phrases.english: And if you say it is just explaining —
but wasn't it taught this way:
We redeem second tithe on an asimon,
these are the words of Rabbi Dosa.
And the Sages say: we do not redeem.
And they agree that we do not redeem

phrases.aramaic: עַל מָעוֹת הַנִּיתָּנוֹת בְּסִימָן לְבֵית הַמֶּרְחָץ!
phrases.english: on coins given as a token for the bathhouse!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects a possible defense of רב and strengthens the challenge in step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the ברייתא's second phrase only explains the word אסימון.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A second ברייתא gives the two items different laws: there is an argument about an אסימון, but everyone agrees about bathhouse tokens.

steps.title: An אסימון is a blank coin
steps.stepSummary: Since רב's answer was pushed away, רבי יוחנן gives a new answer: an אסימון is an unstamped blank.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יוחנן said: What is an אסימון? A blank.
steps.whatsHappening: רב's answer did not hold up, so the גמרא brings a different answer to the question 'what is an אסימון?' רבי יוחנן says it is a blank, a piece of metal shaped like a coin that has no stamp on it yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא tells us the old answer (bathhouse token) is dropped. Now an אסימון is metal that has the shape of a coin but has not been stamped, so it is not yet a working coin.

keyTerms.meaning: A coin-like piece of metal; here, an unstamped blank
A blank: metal shaped like a coin but not yet stamped
Rather: drops the earlier answer and gives a new one

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yochanan said:
What is an asimon? A blank.
phrases.notes: A blank is a piece of metal cut in the shape of a coin, before any picture was stamped on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מַאי אֲסִימוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב's definition, which was knocked down in steps 6-7

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's view fits another statement of his
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבי יוחנן's definition matches his teaching that רבי דוסא and רבי ישמעאל hold the same view.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן follows his own reasoning, as רבי יוחנן said: רבי דוסא and רבי ישמעאל said the same thing. רבי דוסא: what we already said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that this definition fits something else רבי יוחנן said: רבי דוסא and רבי ישמעאל agree. This sets up the next question about where רבי ישמעאל said this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי דוסא, in the ברייתא from step 7, holds that an אסימון works for מעשר שני. If רבי יוחנן says רבי ישמעאל agrees with him, and רבי ישמעאל allows a blank, then רבי יוחנן must understand אסימון as a blank.

keyTerms.meaning: He follows his own reasoning; this fits his other teaching
The same thing; the same opinion

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan follows his own reasoning,
as Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי דּוֹסָא וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אָמְרוּ דָּבָר אֶחָד,
phrases.english: Rabbi Dosa and Rabbi Yishmael said the same thing.
Rabbi Dosa: that which we said.
phrases.notes: This points back to the ברייתא in step 7, where רבי דוסא and the חכמים argue about an אסימון.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 8 by showing it fits another teaching of רבי יוחנן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי דוסא and רבי ישמעאל hold the same view

steps.title: Where is רבי ישמעאל's view?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which statement of רבי ישמעאל is meant.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל: what is it?
steps.whatsHappening: We know where רבי דוסא's view is, so the גמרא asks where רבי ישמעאל said the same thing. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To see that the two agree, we need to see רבי ישמעאל's actual words. The question just asks for the source.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? Which statement is meant?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael, what is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the second half of step 9
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which teaching of רבי ישמעאל matches רבי דוסא

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא on the פסוק of מעשר שני
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי ישמעאל learns from the פסוק that anything held as money counts, and רבי עקיבא says only something with a stamped image counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: 'And you shall bind up the money in your hand': this includes anything that can be bound up in the hand. These are the words of רבי ישמעאל. רבי עקיבא says: it includes anything that has an image on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא with רבי ישמעאל's view. He says anything of value you can hold as money works for מעשר שני, even a blank, while רבי עקיבא requires a stamped coin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל reads וצרת as 'bind up', so anything you can hold works, even with no stamp. רבי עקיבא reads it like צורה, an image, so only a stamped coin works. Since רבי ישמעאל allows a blank, he matches רבי דוסא, who allows an אסימון, and that only works if an אסימון is a blank.

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall bind up the money (פסוק about מעשר שני)
That can be bound up in the hand

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן: an אסימון is a blank. רבי דוסא (who allows an אסימון) and רבי ישמעאל (who allows anything held as money) say the same thing. רבי עקיבא requires a stamp.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:
"And you shall bind up the money in your hand"
to include anything that is bound up in the hand,
the words of Rabbi Yishmael.
Rabbi Akiva says:

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבּוֹת כׇּל דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ עָלָיו צוּרָה.
phrases.english: to include anything that has an image on it.
phrases.notes: רבי עקיבא hears וצרת as sounding like צורה, an image, so he wants a stamped coin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא where רבי ישמעאל allows anything held as money, even without a stamp

steps.title: Back to the משנה: pulling without paying
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: if the buyer pulled the produce but did not pay, he cannot back out.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? If he pulled produce from him but did not give him money, he cannot back out, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה. This sets up רבי יוחנן's explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that משיכה (pulling) is what closes the deal on movable items. Giving money alone does not, so if the buyer paid but did not pull, the deal is not closed and he can still back out.

keyTerms.meaning: Pulled: the act of acquiring movable items
To back out of the deal

phrases.english: How so?
If he pulled produce from him
but did not give him money,
he cannot back out, etc.
phrases.notes: וכו׳ means the משנה goes on: if he paid but did not pull, he can still back out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אסימון topic and opens a new part of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משיכה completes the purchase of movable items; money alone does not

steps.title: By Torah law money acquires; משיכה is a rabbinic decree
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן: by Torah law money acquires. The חכמים made משיכה the way to acquire so the seller won't say 'your wheat burned in the attic.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: By Torah law, money acquires. Why did they say pulling acquires? It is a גזירה, so the seller won't say to the buyer, 'Your wheat burned in the attic.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains the משנה: really, by Torah law, paying money is enough. The חכמים changed this so that only משיכה acquires, because of a worry about fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If money acquired, the wheat would belong to the buyer while it still sat in the seller's attic. If a fire broke out, the seller would not bother to save it and would just say 'your wheat burned.' Keeping it his until the buyer pulls makes him protect it.

keyTerms.meaning: Pulling: acquiring an item by pulling it
A rabbinic decree, made to prevent a problem

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
By Torah law, money acquires,
and why did they say pulling acquires?
It is a decree, lest he say to him
"Your wheat was burned in the attic."
phrases.notes: The seller is the one saying this to the buyer, who already paid but left the wheat at the seller's place.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: דְּבַר תּוֹרָה מָעוֹת קוֹנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind the משנה in step 12
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Money acquires by Torah law; משיכה is a rabbinic גזירה so the seller keeps guarding the goods

steps.title: Whoever started the fire has to pay
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: why worry? Whoever set the fire will have to pay for the wheat anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end, whoever set the fire has to pay!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's reason. If someone caused the fire, he pays, so the buyer does not lose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason in step 13 was that the buyer could lose his wheat. But the person who started the fire must pay for the damage. So the buyer is covered and the גזירה seems unneeded.

phrases.english: In the end,
whoever set the fire has to pay!

steps.triggerLanguage: סוֹף סוֹף, מַאן דִּשְׁדָא דְּלֵיקָה בָּעֵי שַׁלּוֹמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason given in step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason for the גזירה in step 13
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The buyer will be paid by whoever caused the fire, so he has no loss to worry about

steps.title: The worry is an accidental fire
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: the worry is a fire that happens by accident, where no one pays. If the goods are still the seller's, he will work hard to save them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is a גזירה in case a fire breaks out by accident. If you leave the goods in the seller's ownership, he will push himself, work hard, and save them. If not, he will not push himself, work hard, and save them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes רבי יוחנן's reason. The concern is a fire with no one to blame, so nobody pays, and only the seller can save the goods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In an accidental fire (אונס) there is no one to pay, so the קשיא does not apply. The seller only works hard to save things that are his. So the חכמים kept the goods his until משיכה.

keyTerms.meaning: By accident, through no one's fault
He gives himself over, makes a real effort

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, money acquires by Torah law. משיכה is a rabbinic גזירה so the seller will save the goods from an accidental fire.

phrases.english: Rather: it is a decree
lest a fire break out by accident.
If you keep them in his possession,
phrases.notes: "His" means the seller's: the goods still belong to him.

phrases.english: he will give himself over, work hard, and save them.
And if not,
he will not give himself over, work hard, and save them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא תִּפּוֹל דְּלֵיקָה בְּאוֹנֶס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the worry is only about an accidental fire
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The worry was any fire, even one someone caused, where the one at fault would pay
steps.terutzMaskana: The worry is an accidental fire with no one to pay, so only the seller's effort can save the goods

steps.title: ריש לקיש: משיכה is from the Torah
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש disagrees: משיכה is written clearly in the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: משיכה is stated clearly in the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives the opposite view from רבי יוחנן. He says משיכה is the Torah's way of acquiring movable items, not a rabbinic גזירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, money acquires by Torah law and משיכה was added by the חכמים. For ריש לקיש, משיכה itself is the Torah law. This is a real argument about where משיכה comes from.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
Pulling is stated explicitly in the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: מְשִׁיכָה מְפוֹרֶשֶׁת מִן הַתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי יוחנן in step 13
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משיכה is the Torah's way of acquiring movable items

steps.title: What is ריש לקיש's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what ריש לקיש bases himself on.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of ריש לקיש?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where in the Torah ריש לקיש sees משיכה. This sets up the פסוק that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש said משיכה is 'clearly in the Torah,' so the גמרא wants to see the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason or source?

phrases.english: What is the reason of Reish Lakish?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of step 16
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that shows משיכה is from the Torah

steps.title: The פסוק: acquired from hand to hand
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש learns from 'or acquire from your colleague's hand' that the Torah means something passed from hand to hand, which is משיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And if you sell something to your colleague, or acquire from your colleague's hand': something that is acquired from hand to hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives ריש לקיש's source. The words 'from your colleague's hand' show that a purchase happens when the item passes from hand to hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah describes buying as taking the item from the seller's hand. Moving the item from one person to the other is משיכה. So for ריש לקיש, משיכה is the Torah's way of acquiring.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן: money acquires by Torah law, and משיכה is a גזירה. ריש לקיש: משיכה is from the Torah, learned from 'from your colleague's hand.'

phrases.english: The verse says:
"And if you sell something to your colleague
or acquire from your colleague's hand,"
something that is acquired from hand to hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: וְכִי תִמְכְּרוּ מִמְכָּר לַעֲמִיתֶךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'or acquire from your colleague's hand' shows acquisition from hand to hand, which is משיכה

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: 'From the hand' excludes land
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the word 'מיד' is not about משיכה. It comes to exclude קרקע, which has no אונאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: 'From the hand' comes to exclude land, which is not subject to the law of exploitation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us how רבי יוחנן reads the same word that ריש לקיש just used to prove משיכה. For רבי יוחנן, 'from the hand' teaches something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש said 'from your colleague's hand' points to something passed hand to hand, which is משיכה. רבי יוחנן agrees the word points to things passed by hand, but he uses it to exclude land, which cannot be handed over. So land is left out of the rules of אונאה, and the פסוק says nothing about משיכה.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude; to leave something out of the rule
Overcharging or underpaying; cheating someone on the price

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
"From the hand" comes to exclude land,
which is not subject to exploitation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יוחנן's different reading of the same word ריש לקיש used for משיכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'מיד' excludes קרקע from the laws of אונאה. It is not a source for משיכה.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: 'Or acquire' would be extra, so it teaches pulling
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that if 'מיד' only excluded land, the פסוק could have left out 'או קנה'. Since those words are there, they teach משיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש? If so, let the verse write: 'And if you sell an item from your colleague's hand, do not exploit.' Why do I need 'or acquire'? Learn from it that acquisition is by pulling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how ריש לקיש answers רבי יוחנן's reading. He says the words 'או קנה' are extra, and extra words must teach משיכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש accepts that the פסוק excludes land. He argues that for that lesson alone, the פסוק could have said 'sell from your colleague's hand' without adding 'or acquire'. The added words connect 'acquiring' to 'from the hand', which shows that Torah-level קנין for movable items is done by משיכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? (the word seems extra)
Pulling an item toward oneself to acquire it

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish (how does he answer)?
If so, let the verse write:
"And if you sell an item
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:14. ריש לקיש is rewriting the פסוק without 'or acquire' to show those words are extra.

phrases.english: from your colleague's hand, do not exploit,"
why do I need "or acquire"?
Learn from it: it teaches pulling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוחנן's reading by pointing to the extra words 'או קנה'.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How does ריש לקיש answer רבי יוחנן's reading of 'מיד'?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra words 'או קנה' would be unnecessary for excluding land alone, so they must teach משיכה.

steps.title: What does רבי יוחנן do with 'or acquire'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי יוחנן learns from the words 'או קנה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן: what does he do with 'or acquire'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to רבי יוחנן and asks what the words 'או קנה' teach in his view. This sets up the next step, where it will answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש's argument was that 'או קנה' must teach something. רבי יוחנן does not use those words for משיכה, so he needs a different lesson from them.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he do with it? (what does he learn from it)
'Or acquire': words from the פסוק of אונאה

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan:
what does he do with "or acquire"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns ריש לקיש's point back on רבי יוחנן: what do the extra words teach him?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson רבי יוחנן learns from 'או קנה'.

steps.title: 'Or acquire' teaches that cheating the seller is also forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן uses 'או קנה' for a ברייתא's lesson: אונאה is forbidden even when the seller is the one who loses.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for what is taught in a ברייתא: 'And if you sell an item, do not exploit.' This only teaches when the buyer was cheated. From where do we know when the seller was cheated? The verse says: 'Or acquire, do not exploit.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן needs 'או קנה' for a ברייתא. Those words teach that the buyer may not cheat the seller.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part of the פסוק, 'if you sell', speaks to the seller. It warns him not to overcharge the buyer. The words 'or acquire' speak to the buyer and warn him not to underpay the seller. So for רבי יוחנן these words are not extra, and he has no source for משיכה here.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (for a different lesson)
As it is taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: He needs it for what is taught in a baraita:
"And if you sell an item, do not exploit":
I only know this when the buyer was cheated;
from where do we know when the seller was cheated?
The verse says: "Or acquire, do not exploit."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21 by giving 'או קנה' its own lesson.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'או קנה' teaches that אונאה applies when the seller is cheated, so it is not extra and does not teach משיכה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It establishes that the איסור of אונאה works in both directions: the seller may not overcharge, and the buyer may not underpay.

steps.title: ריש לקיש learns both lessons from 'or acquire'
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש learns two things from 'או קנה': אונאה of the seller, and משיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש? He learns two things from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that ריש לקיש also accepts the ברייתא's lesson about cheating the seller. He learns both that lesson and משיכה from the same words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might ask how ריש לקיש can use 'או קנה' for משיכה if רבי יוחנן needs it for the seller's אונאה. The answer is that ריש לקיש draws both lessons from the phrase 'או קנה מיד עמיתך'. So the disagreement stays in place: ריש לקיש has a Torah source for משיכה, and רבי יוחנן does not.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן: 'מיד' excludes קרקע, and 'או קנה' teaches that cheating the seller is forbidden, so there is no Torah source for משיכה. ריש לקיש: 'או קנה מיד עמיתך' teaches both the seller's אונאה and משיכה.

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish (where does he learn the seller's case)?
He learns two things from it.
phrases.notes: From 'or acquire' he learns both that the seller is protected and that buying is done by pulling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that ריש לקיש accepts the ברייתא of step 22 and still keeps his reading of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ריש לקיש learns both the seller's אונאה and משיכה from the same phrase.

steps.title: Challenge to ריש לקיש from רבי שמעון in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says only the seller can back out once money is paid. That fits the view that money acquires, but seems to contradict ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: רבי שמעון says, whoever holds the money has the upper hand. The seller can back out, but the buyer cannot. That makes sense if money acquires. But if money does not acquire, the buyer should also be able to back out!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the opinion of רבי שמעון in the משנה to attack ריש לקיש, who holds that money does not acquire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוחנן, money acquires by Torah law, and the חכמים added משיכה only to protect the buyer. So only the seller gets a way out, which is exactly what רבי שמעון says. According to ריש לקיש, nothing has been acquired yet, so both sides should be equally free to back out.

keyTerms.meaning: His hand is on top: he has the upper hand
Money acquires: paying makes the sale final
It works well (one side fits, the other is hard)

phrases.english: We learned: Rabbi Shimon says:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁהַכֶּסֶף בְּיָדוֹ – יָדוֹ עַל הָעֶלְיוֹנָה.
phrases.english: Whoever has the money in his hand, his hand is on top.
phrases.notes: The one holding the money is the seller, who has already been paid.

phrases.english: It is the seller who can back out,
the buyer cannot back out.
It works well if you say money acquires:

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם הָכִי מוֹכֵר מָצֵי הָדַר בֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: that is why the seller can back out,
and the buyer cannot back out.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ מָעוֹת אֵינָן קוֹנוֹת –
phrases.english: But if you say money does not acquire,
then the buyer should also be able to back out!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the derivations from the פסוק, the גמרא tests ריש לקיש's view against a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that money does not acquire movables
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון gives an advantage only to the seller. That only makes sense if the buyer is already bound by paying, meaning money acquires.

steps.title: ריש לקיש follows the רבנן, not רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש admits רבי שמעון disagrees with him. He says his own view follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש can tell you: I did not say my view according to רבי שמעון. I said it according to the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers the challenge by saying his view follows the other opinion in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש does not try to fit רבי שמעון into his view. He accepts that רבי שמעון holds money acquires. He says the רבנן argue with רבי שמעון, and his own rule follows the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: He can tell you (an answer given on his behalf)
The Sages who argue with רבי שמעון in the משנה

phrases.english: Reish Lakish can tell you:
I did not say it according to Rabbi Shimon;
when I said it, it was according to the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the view to the other side of a מחלוקת
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ריש לקיש's view seemed to clash with the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: It clashes only with רבי שמעון. ריש לקיש follows the רבנן.

steps.title: What do רבי שמעון and the רבנן argue about according to רבי יוחנן?
steps.stepSummary: For ריש לקיש the argument is clear: does money acquire or not? For רבי יוחנן, who holds money acquires, the גמרא asks what the two sides disagree about.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for ריש לקיש: that is the difference between רבי שמעון and the רבנן. But according to רבי יוחנן, what is the difference between רבי שמעון and the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to רבי יוחנן and asks him to explain what the מחלוקת in the משנה is about. It is setting up the next step's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Following ריש לקיש, רבי שמעון holds money acquires and the רבנן hold it does not. רבי יוחנן says money acquires according to everyone, so the argument needs a new explanation.

phrases.english: It works well according to Reish Lakish:

phrases.aramaic: הַיְינוּ דְּאִיכָּא בֵּין רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לְרַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: that is the difference between Rabbi Shimon and the Rabbis.
But according to Rabbi Yochanan,

phrases.aramaic: מַאי אִיכָּא בֵּין רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לְרַבָּנַן?
phrases.english: what difference is there between Rabbi Shimon and the Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since ריש לקיש explained the מחלוקת through his view, the גמרא asks how רבי יוחנן explains it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The point of disagreement between רבי שמעון and the רבנן, according to רבי יוחנן

steps.title: They argue about רב חסדא's rule
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי יוחנן, the argument is whether the חכמים' rule of משיכה also lets the buyer back out, as רב חסדא says.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is רב חסדא's rule. רב חסדא said: Just as the חכמים made משיכה a requirement for sellers, they made it a requirement for buyers. רבי שמעון does not hold like רב חסדא. The רבנן do hold like רב חסדא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: according to רבי יוחנן, רבי שמעון and the רבנן argue about רב חסדא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees money acquires by Torah law. The question is how far the חכמים' rule of משיכה goes. The רבנן say that before משיכה the buyer can also back out. רבי שמעון says only the seller can.

keyTerms.meaning: Does not hold of / does hold of

phrases.english: Between them is the rule of Rav Chisda.
For Rav Chisda said:
Just as they instituted pulling for sellers,
so they instituted pulling for buyers.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לֵית לֵיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon does not hold of Rav Chisda's rule,
the Rabbis do hold of Rav Chisda's rule.

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש: רבי שמעון and the רבנן argue whether money acquires. רבי יוחנן: everyone agrees money acquires by Torah law; they argue whether the חכמים let the buyer back out too (רב חסדא).
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: According to רבי יוחנן, they argue about רב חסדא's rule that משיכה was also instituted for buyers.

steps.title: Challenge to ריש לקיש from the מי שפרע curse
steps.stepSummary: The משנה curses someone who backs out after payment. That makes sense if money acquires, but why curse him if nothing was acquired?
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: But they said, He Who punished the generation of the flood will one day punish whoever does not keep his word. That makes sense if money acquires, so he falls under the curse. But if money does not acquire, why does he fall under the curse?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge against ריש לקיש, this time from the curse of מי שפרע in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If money acquires by Torah law, backing out means undoing a real sale, so a harsh curse fits. If money does not acquire, as ריש לקיש says, no sale has happened yet, so whoever backs out has not undone anything by Torah law. Then the curse seems out of place.

keyTerms.meaning: Stands under the curse that starts with 'But they said'

phrases.english: We learned: But they said,
He Who punished the generation of the flood
will in the future punish
whoever does not stand by his word.
It works well if you say money acquires:
that is why he stands under the "But",
phrases.notes: The "But" is short for the curse in the משנה, which opens with "But they said."

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ מָעוֹת אֵינָן קוֹנוֹת,
phrases.english: but if you say money does not acquire,
why does he stand under the "But"?

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: אֲבָל אָמְרוּ, מִי שֶׁפָּרַע מִדּוֹר הַמַּבּוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge against ריש לקיש, from a different line of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that money does not acquire movables
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A curse for backing out suggests the sale was already real, meaning money acquires.

steps.title: The curse is for breaking his word
steps.stepSummary: The curse is not because a sale was undone. It is because he broke the promise he made.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is because of words.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for ריש לקיש: the curse is for going back on his spoken commitment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if nothing was acquired, the person agreed to the deal and was paid. Breaking that word is enough to bring the curse, so the curse does not prove that money acquires.

phrases.english: Because of words.
phrases.notes: He agreed to the deal and then went back on what he said.

steps.confusionAlert: The curse does not mean a sale took place. Under this answer, it only means he broke his word.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the reason for the ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The curse shows that money made the sale final.
steps.terutzMaskana: The curse is for breaking a spoken commitment, even without an acquisition.

steps.title: Does breaking a verbal promise really bring the curse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer of Step 29. It asks whether someone who goes back on words alone is really included in the משנה's curse that opens with "אבל אמרו", and it begins to quote a ברייתא as evidence.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is someone who backs out of mere words really included in the "But" (the curse of מי שפרע)? But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is questioning the answer just given, that the curse is for breaking a promise. This line sets up the next move: a ברייתא will be quoted to show the answer has a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 29 said the curse is for breaking one's word. The גמרא now doubts that going back on words alone, with no real acquisition behind it, is serious enough for the curse of מי שפרע. The word "וְהָתַנְיָא" tells us a ברייתא is coming that seems to say otherwise.

keyTerms.meaning: Mere words, a verbal promise without a real act of acquiring
Does he stand under? Is he really included in?
"But". This is the opening word of the משנה's curse: "אבל אמרו מי שפרע"

steps.confusionAlert: "אבל" here is not just the ordinary word "but." It is the גמרא's short way of naming the משנה's curse, which begins "אבל אמרו מי שפרע".

phrases.english: And for mere words, does one stand under the "But"?
phrases.notes: "The But" means the משנה's curse, which opens with the words "אבל אמרו מי שפרע".

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of Step 29, which explained the curse as being for breaking one's word.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 29 that the curse of מי שפרע applies to someone who goes back on mere words.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Going back on words alone may not be serious enough for the curse of מי שפרע, and a ברייתא is about to be brought to show this, so the answer of Step 29 looks weak.
